input_signals.name: Supplier-Independent Gross Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(apalch, LAG(at, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability is more durable when it is not supported by increasing accounts payable and accrued liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: An increase in apalch represents supplier or liability financing that can temporarily support operating cash flow without improving underlying economics. Focusing on this specific financing channel, rather than aggregate working-capital accruals, rewards profitable firms that are not relying on delayed payments.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( apalch, lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Release Core Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), at)), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(recch, LAG(at, 1))), IND_RANK(RATIO(invch, LAG(at, 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Strong core operating profit is more credible when neither receivables nor inventory is accumulating.
input_signals.reasoning: Compustat recch and invch are signed as decreases minus increases, so high values correctly indicate cash release rather than asset accumulation. The minimum operator prevents a receivables decrease from offsetting an inventory buildup, requiring both accrual channels to corroborate reported profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), at ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( recch, lag( at, 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( invch, lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Liquid Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(che, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profitability is more credible when it coincides with cash accumulation or short-term debt repayment.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in cash alone may be financed by new borrowing, so the accrual-quality leg measures the change in cash net of short-term debt. A high score requires both profitable operations and an improving net-liquid position, consistent with internally realized earnings.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( delta( sub( che, dlc ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded EBITDA Improvement
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: EBITDA improvement accompanied by increased short-term borrowing predicts subsequent underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests financing dependence rather than supplier or operating-liability accruals: improving profitability is less credible when the firm must simultaneously increase short-term debt. The signed, industry-standardized debt change creates a two-sided contrast between borrowing and debt repayment, while profitability improvement determines the strength of that contrast.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( ebitda, at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Share-Verified Core Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt)), IND_ZSCORE(DELTA(RATIO(che, act), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Strong core operating margins are more durable when cash is increasing as a share of current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: A rising cash share indicates that current assets are rotating away from receivables, inventory, and other accrual-bearing balances toward realized liquidity. The bounded cash-to-current-assets denominator avoids the instability of dividing profit by a potentially tiny noncash-asset balance, while the signed interaction prevents core margin from acting as a standalone profitability signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ) ), ind_zscore( delta( ratio( che, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Share-Confirmed Margin Trend
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(che, act), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving core operating margins are more durable when cash persistently rises as a share of current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Joint trends test whether margin improvement is accompanied by a sustained balance-sheet rotation from accrual-bearing current assets toward cash. Requiring both trends to rank highly may produce cleaner portfolio tails than combining a profitability level with a noisy one-period cash-share change.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( che, act ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Harvest
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), MIN(IND_RANK(LAG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), LAG(at, 1))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms should outperform when a prior working-capital investment is currently reversing and releasing cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal targets a realization cycle rather than the familiar level or contemporaneous change in working capital: prior investment must be followed by a current release. High operating profitability helps distinguish productive cash harvesting from working-capital liquidation caused by business contraction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), min( ind_rank( lag( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Cash-Floor Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(che, act), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained profitability is more durable when firms maintain a consistently high cash share of current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: A three-period cash floor distinguishes persistent liquidity backing from a temporary cash increase caused by financing or reporting-date timing. The bottleneck structure requires both sustained EBITDA profitability and consistently low dependence on accrual-bearing current assets, rather than mechanically negating an archived liquidity-change signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( ebitda, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( che, act ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Interest Timing Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), LAG(at, 1)), DELTA(RATIO(xint, at), 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High pretax profitability is less durable when short-term debt rises without a commensurate increase in recognized interest expense.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal targets a specific timing mismatch: newly accumulated debt can create a future cash and earnings burden before its full interest cost appears in current results. Weighting the industry-standardized debt-interest gap by pretax profitability identifies firms whose apparently strong earnings are most exposed to that delayed financing cost.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( pi, at ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( sub( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), delta( ratio( xint, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Operating Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, SUB(lct, dlc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent operating profitability is more credible when cash can cover a large share of non-debt current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Non-debt current liabilities represent supplier, employee, and other accrued operating claims that eventually require settlement. The bounded coverage ratio avoids unstable near-zero denominators, and the bottleneck structure rewards profits supported by the capacity to settle those accrual obligations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, sub( lct, dlc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Capital-Efficient Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins are more durable when firms require progressively fewer noncash current assets per dollar of revenue.
input_signals.reasoning: Declining noncash-current-asset intensity indicates improving collections, inventory efficiency, or reduced dependence on other accrual-bearing operating assets. Combining that trend with sustained margins targets profitable firms whose earnings require less accrual capital rather than merely firms with a high static profitability ratio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Declining Nondepreciation Accrual Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(ADD(SUB(ib, oancf), dpc), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent EBITDA profitability is more durable when nondepreciation accrual reliance is declining.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding dpc to income minus operating cash flow removes the depreciation component and isolates working-capital and other nondepreciation accruals. Pairing that trend with EBITDA avoids double-penalizing depreciation and tests whether sustained pre-depreciation profitability increasingly converts into cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( ebitda, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( add( sub( ib, oancf ), dpc ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Debt-Service Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(pi, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(dlc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained pretax profitability is more credible when operating cash flow is strong relative to short-term debt requiring repayment or refinancing.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces debt-issuance timing with a debt-service-capacity mechanism, avoiding the telescoping growth term that can proxy for asset expansion. The bounded cash-coverage ratio rewards positive operating cash flow relative to current debt, while the bottleneck requires profitability and repayment capacity to be jointly strong.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( pi, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( oancf, add( abs( oancf ), abs( dlc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitable Debt-Interest State Gap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(xint, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms with unusually high short-term debt intensity relative to recognized interest-cost intensity should underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the successful change-based timing signal, this tests a balance-sheet state in which the financing obligation is already large but its income-statement burden remains unusually small. Separately standardizing debt and interest intensity avoids arbitrary stock-flow weighting and removes direct exposure to debt issuance or multi-year asset growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( pi, at ) ), sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( xint, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Capital Efficiency Breakout
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(SUB(LAG(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt), 3), 1), RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins should be especially durable when noncash current assets per dollar of revenue fall below their prior historical floor.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal identifies a discrete improvement in accrual-capital requirements rather than simply repeating their recent trend. Requiring sustained margins alongside a new efficiency low helps distinguish structural cash-conversion improvement from noncash-asset contraction caused by deteriorating operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sub( lag( ts_min( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ), 3 ), 1 ), ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Settled Cost Efficiency
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(xsga, revt), 1))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(che, ADD(che, SUB(lct, dlc))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Reductions in SG&A intensity are more durable when the firm's cash coverage of accrued operating liabilities improves concurrently.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier liability-funded cost signal failed because increasing operating liabilities may reflect financing rather than expense manipulation. This formulation instead asks whether apparent cost efficiency improves the firm's ability to settle operating claims, linking the profit source directly to a cash-backed balance-sheet outcome.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( xsga, revt ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( che, add( che, sub( lct, dlc ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Investment-Covered Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(ABS(oancf), MAX(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), SUB(at, at))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profitability is more durable when operating cash flow is sufficient to cover contemporaneous investment in noncash current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: The quality leg measures cash generation relative to positive accrual investment, while treating a noncash-current-asset release as supportive rather than penalizing its absolute magnitude. Its bounded construction avoids the archived cash-share-change leg and directly tests whether profitable operations fund their additional receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( oancf, add( abs( oancf ), max( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), sub( at, at ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Balanced Operating-Accrual Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(ABS(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(TREND(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), revt), 3)))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins are more durable when changes in noncash operating assets are matched by corresponding changes in non-debt operating liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal rewards balance between the two sides of the operating accrual cycle rather than mechanically favoring a high operating-liability share or a low net-working-capital level. Both unmatched asset expansion that absorbs cash and unmatched liability expansion that may reflect payment stretching receive low accrual-quality scores.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( abs( sub( ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( trend( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), revt ), 3 ) ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low Accrual-Capital Ceiling
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(act, che), revt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins are more durable when noncash current assets per dollar of revenue remain consistently low.
input_signals.reasoning: The historical maximum measures the firm's worst recent dependence on receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets. Unlike the successful trend and breakout signals, this construction tests whether a permanently low accrual-capital ceiling identifies profitable firms with structurally superior cash conversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( sub( act, che ), revt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low-Opaque-Accrual Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ABS(aoloch), ADD(ABS(aoloch), ABS(oancf))), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent operating profitability is more durable when unclassified other operating asset and liability adjustments are a small share of operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Large aoloch adjustments indicate that reported cash conversion depends on opaque accrual channels outside the standard receivables, inventory, and payable components. The bounded magnitude ratio is sign-agnostic and rewards profitable firms whose operating cash flow requires fewer unclassified accounting adjustments.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ma( ratio( abs( aoloch ), add( abs( aoloch ), abs( oancf ) ) ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Stress-Tested Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(dpc, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High after-depreciation operating profitability is especially credible when depreciation intensity is elevated relative to the firm's own history.
input_signals.reasoning: The within-firm depreciation rank controls for persistent capital-intensity differences and identifies periods when the accounting charge presents an unusually demanding hurdle. A high score requires profitability to remain strong after that elevated charge, avoiding the prior construction's subtraction of dpc from cash flow and its resulting double penalty.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ts_rank( ratio( dpc, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Covered Financing Claims
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(pi, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, ADD(ABS(dlc), ABS(xint))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained pretax profitability is more durable when available cash can cover short-term debt and its associated interest burden.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the previously tested debt-interest timing anomaly with a financing-claim settlement-capacity mechanism. The bounded ratio compares cash with principal and interest claims that can pressure near-term earnings, avoiding exposure to debt issuance growth and removing the assumption that an interest-recognition lag is concealed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( pi, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, add( abs( dlc ), abs( xint ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Reconciled Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(ABS(SUB(dp, dpc)), at), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent after-depreciation profitability is more credible when income-statement depreciation and the cash-flow-statement depreciation addback reconcile closely.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual-quality leg measures reporting consistency rather than the level, trend, or historical rank of depreciation intensity. Large persistent discrepancies can indicate unusual amortization, reclassification, or nonrecurring adjustments that make reported operating profitability harder to interpret.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ma( ratio( abs( sub( dp, dpc ) ), at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory-Confirmed Gross-Margin Expansion
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(invch, LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-margin expansion is more durable when it is accompanied by inventory reduction rather than inventory accumulation.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier adverse inventory conditional produced weak and sign-inconsistent evidence, so this construction instead forms a quality long leg requiring both margin improvement and positive inventory cash contribution. Because invch is decrease minus increase, high values correctly identify inventory release and reduce concern that expanding margins reflect unsold production or deferred costs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( invch, lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt-Independent Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(pi, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(dlc, lct), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent pretax profitability is more durable when short-term debt is declining as a share of total current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests the composition of near-term obligations rather than another cash-coverage denominator or debt-interest timing gap. A declining interest-bearing share indicates that profitable operations are becoming less dependent on short-maturity external financing and its associated rollover risk.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( pi, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( dlc, lct ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Collection-Backed Margin
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(NEG(recch), DELTA(revt, 1)), LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins are more durable when receivables growth does not exceed contemporaneous revenue growth.
input_signals.reasoning: The collection-confirmed margin-change signal produced aligned but only moderate evidence, while persistent profitability levels have generated stronger portfolio results elsewhere in the archive. This construction tests whether abnormal customer-credit expansion is most informative when separating durable high-margin firms rather than one-year margin movers.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( winsor( ratio( sub( neg( recch ), delta( revt, 1 ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Customer-Funded Core Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, ADD(cogs, xsga)), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(recch, apalch), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent core margins are more credible when operating cash support comes from customer collections rather than increased supplier financing.
input_signals.reasoning: Positive recch reflects receivables reduction, while positive apalch reflects increased payables or accrued liabilities; their difference separates customer-funded cash realization from payment deferral. This source-of-cash mechanism is distinct from combining aggregate operating and financing claim-coverage ratios.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, add( cogs, xsga ) ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( recch, apalch ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory-Efficient Gross-Profit Growth
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(invch, LAG(at, 1)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Inventory release is favorable when total gross profit is growing, indicating efficient conversion rather than distress liquidation.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross-profit growth incorporates both sales volume and margin, directly addressing the prior portfolio contamination from high-margin firms shrinking inventory during contraction. A high score therefore requires inventory cash release and an expanding gross-profit pool rather than merely a strong or improving margin percentage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( invch, lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fully Burdened Pretax Profit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), MIN(IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(dpc, at), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, ADD(che, ADD(ABS(dlc), ABS(xint)))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Pretax profitability is especially credible when it remains high under an elevated depreciation burden and strong financing-claim coverage.
input_signals.reasoning: Pretax income already reflects depreciation and interest, so high profitability under both an unusually demanding capital-consumption charge and well-covered financing obligations represents a jointly stress-tested outcome. The construction combines two economically related burdens rather than adding a low-information depreciation-reconciliation tie breaker.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( pi, at ) ), min( ind_rank( ts_rank( ratio( dpc, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, add( che, add( abs( dlc ), abs( xint ) ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Standardized Accrual-Investment Payoff
input_signals.expression: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(LAG(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(revt, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should outperform when operating-profit improvement exceeds the standardized prior excess investment in noncash current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: The outer standardization gives the lagged two-channel excess-investment composite the same cross-sectional scale as profit improvement, preventing it from mechanically dominating the spread. The resulting signal directly measures realized profit response relative to growth-adjusted accrual investment rather than treating raw excess accruals as the outcome.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( ind_zscore( winsor( delta( ratio( oibdp, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( lag( sub( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( act, che ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( revt, 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low Rollover-Risk Profitability
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(pi, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MAX(RATIO(dlc, lct), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent pretax profitability is more durable when short-term debt never becomes a large share of current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces two highly collinear cash-coverage ratios with a financing-composition ceiling that does not depend on cash holdings. The historical maximum identifies sustained exposure to rollover-sensitive debt, while allowing profitable firms with consistently low short-term borrowing dependence to form a broad quality long leg.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: Stable Accrual-Capital Margin
